children: Chinese oil stocks are broadly higher in Shanghai and Hong Kong, after oil prices rallied overnight. Renewed hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Houthi militants in Yemen are raising concerns about the security of Red Sea shipping routes, pushing oil prices higher. Front-month Brent crude rose 3.5% on Wednesday and is last 0.1% higher. West Texas Intermediate crude rises 0.4% in early trading after gaining 2% in the previous session. China's three oil majors strengthen in Hong Kong and Shanghai. PetroChina, Sinopec and Cnooc gain 4.3%, 1.9% and 4.4%, respectively, in Hong Kong, and rise 2.1%, 1.2% and 3.3%, respectively, in Shanghai. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
